An Aadhaar number is a digital biometric identity issued voluntarily to residents of India, it can also be issued in card form, but it is not compulsory either. Proof of identity such as a passport, Aadhaar, ration card, PAN card, or driving licence is mandatory for issuing es…
Normally this is first issued at school age, but it can be issued whenever the legal ascendant(s) request its issue

The card is issued to Indonesian citizens and foreign nationals with permanent residence in the Republic of Indonesia. Possession of KTP is compulsory for residents whose age is 17 or older, and residents who is married before the age of 17
The CNIC with a unique 13 digit identification number can be applied for aged 18 and above
Compulsory to be issued since the age of 18
"National Identity" (NID) card is a compulsory electronic biometric identification for all citizens at the age of 18 and above

A Russian identity document is issued to any citizen on request at the age of 14 and reissued at ages 20 and 45. People may use other documents for identity as well (e.g., driver's license, passport), but only in limited number of cases. Banks, post offices and authority offic…

A foundational digital ID, that focuses on a unique number (instead of a card), and this unique number, known as Fayda Identification Number is the primary identifier and essentially serves as a legal ID
This card is required to participate in Federal level elections and while it is the de facto ID for most legal transactions, it is not mandatory to have one
An Individual Number Card is issued to citizens of Japan as well as legal residents. It was introducted in 2016 and replaces the Juki-Card
The Personality Verification Card is compulsory at the age of 16. Not carrying the ID card is only penalised by fine not exceeding £E200

The Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) ID also known as the Philippine identity card is issued to all Filipino citizens and resident aliens in the Philippines. The pilot implementation began in selected regions in 2018 and full implementation began in 2019

All citizens above 14 years old must possess a citizen identification card (latest version is an electronic ID card), provided by the local authority, and must be reissued when the citizens' years of age reach 25, 40 and 60. Formerly a people's ID document was used
Compulsory from birth and must be carried at all times. A photograph is optional until the bearer turns 15. It is often photocopied at government offices, banks, and the like

Compulsory for all German citizens aged 16 or older to possess either a "Personalausweis" (identity card) or a passport, but not to carry it. While police officers and some other officials have a right to demand to see one of those documents, the law does not state that one is…

Compulsory for citizens who are 7 – 70 years of age. People older than 70 years and exempted citizen can still apply for a card. A fee of ฿100 is payable in case of loss, damage or information alteration
Identity cards were introduced on a limited voluntary basis in 2009 under the Identity Cards Act 2006
The country has had a national ID card since 1940, when it helped the Vichy authorities identify 76,000 for deportation as part of the Holocaust.
Compulsory for citizens 16 and older, and compulsory for all non-citizen permanent residents. The older form of Identity Document, in the form of a green booklet, began being phased out in 2013

The Italian electronic identity card may be issued to anyone who is resident in Italy and to Italian citizens living abroad. A card issued to an Italian citizen is accepted in lieu of a passport in all Europe (except in Belarus, Russia and Ukraine) and in Turkey, Georgia, Egyp…
All citizens (and permanent residents) are issued a national identification card at age 18. As at November 2023, IDs in Kenya cost about 2000 shillings (approx. $13.20)
Myanmar citizens are required to have a Citizenship Scrutiny Card
Tarjeta de identidad is issued aged 7. From 26 June 2013, is available the new format (coloured sky blue) with biometric features
Compulsory for all Rwandan citizens living in the country, with a price of 1500 RWF. Valid for international travel to Kenya and Uganda
Compulsory for all Algerian nationals and costs 2500 Algerian Dinar.
Compulsory for anyone 14 and older. Minors younger than 14 can obtain a DNI, for example, to travel to other European countries
Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI) is issued at a person's birth, and updated at 8 and 14 years of age, and thereafter renewed every fifteen years
More than 12 million Angolans do not possess a national identity card

Compulsory for citizens 14 and older. Before 2016, the national identity card was a blue soft paper booklet like the typical international passport. In 2016, the government began issuing credit-card-sized biometric identity cards (a/k/a "internal passport" or "passport card") …

This is an official document which allows any citizen to prove his identity and therefore it is valid, his Moroccan nationality. It is compulsory for all citizens aged over 16 years, but it can be obtained at all ages

At 18, Polish citizens with their permanent residence in Poland must obtain Polish National Identity Card, however at 13 years of age some form of identification is required. The ID Card is issued free of charge
National identity card have officially Uzbek passports internally in 2021
Issued at age 12, and updated at 18
Compulsory for men 17 and older and optional for teenage men aged 15–16. Optional for women but issued to women 18 and older. Compulsory for citizens, expatriates, and residents

National Document of Identification or Documento Nacional de Identidad (DNI). Citizens can have a minor DNI but at the age of 17 they are encouraged to renew their DNI to get an Adult DNI. At 18, it is compulsory
Possession is compulsory for Malagasy citizens from age 18
Optional, although compulsory for voting, acquisition of both passports and driving licenses and for certain government transactions
New biometric cards rolled out in 2018. Information displayed in both English and Nepali
Compulsory for anyone 10 and older, and it must be renewed every 10 years

North Korea is probably the country which imposes the strongest fines for citizens not carrying ID cards. For travel, North Koreans need both an identity card, and a "travel pass", with specified destination and written permission
Compulsory for all Syrian citizens. Must be uptained at the age of 14. Information displayed in Arabic only

All citizens over the age of 16 need to apply for a National Identity Card (NIC), all citizens are required to carry their NIC on them at all times as proof of identity, given the security situation in the country
Compulsory for ROC nationals 14 and older whose household is registered in Taiwan
Biometric. Distribution of national ID cards started in 2017 and the card is compulsory for all national citizens aged 16 and above
Compulsory for citizens aged 16 and older. It is laminated and must be carried at all times
The identity cards have been issued since 1994 and compulsory for all citizens at age 16. Biometric since 2009
Compulsory for all Somali citizens. Electronic since 2014
Normally this is first issued at age 2 or 3, but it can be issued whenever the legal ascendant(s) request its issue. It is compulsory at 18, when it has to be carried at all times
Compulsory for all citizens. Biometric since 2017
Identity cards are issued to any Guatemalan and legal residents. For children between 0 and 12 years the document is golden shaded; between 13 and 17 years the document is silvered
The Carte de identitate is compulsory at 14

Since 1 January 2005 it is compulsory to show identification, when an authorized officer asks for it, from the age of 14. An authorized officer can only do so under certain circumstances. Such circumstances include suspicious behaviour, committing any offence, or if a person i…
Every citizen over 18 years must have a national identity card. The renewal of the card is $10.00
Compulsory for citizens 16 and older. It is plastic and must be carried at all times
Compulsory for all Rwandan citizens living in the country, with a price of 1500 RWF. Valid for international travel to Kenya and Uganda
Valid for international travel within the East African Community
Compulsory at 18, but rarely required by police.
Issued to every South Sudanese of at least eighteen years of age for purposes of employment or as required by a “competent authority.”
Compulsory for citizens 18 and older. A minor can obtain a national identity card with a legal ascendant(s) approval
The card is first issued at age 12, compulsory by 15. Since the beginning of 2005 the eID (electronic IDentity card) has been issued to Belgian citizens who apply for a new identity card
If needed, an underage ID card may be obtained at the age of 16, yet the official ID (which will allow the individual to vote) is obtained at 18
First issued at age 16 and is compulsory by 18
Compulsory for citizens, expatriates and residents. This is also known as Emirates ID
The Honduran national identity card is an electronic ID card, compulsory for all Honduran nationals at the age of 18
Compulsory for all Tajik citizens. Electronic, with informations displayed in both Tajik and English since 2015
Compulsory for anyone 16 and older and must be carried at all times. It is routinely used for identification and is often necessary to conduct public and private business
Having an identity card in Sweden is not mandatory, but it is needed in several situations, e.g. for bank services or when picking up a package at a post office
Compulsory at 15 for those with a permanent stay registered in the country
The Şəxsiyyət vəsiqəsi is an ID card, compulsory upon 16 years old and costs 5 manats (€2,5). It is not compulsory to carry it at all time

As of 2006 the government has issued the Cartão do Cidadão (Citizen Card). The older Bilhete de identidade which has been compulsory at 10, is still in limited use. All citizens starting at the age of 6 are required to obtain an identity card, but are not required to carry them
Police ID is the only legal identity document and no one has a right to ask for more identity documents. Since the 1980s all legal services in Greece must be done with this ID
The Teudat Zehut is first issued at age 16 and is compulsory by 18
It is compulsory to possess an Személyi igazolvány (Identity card) or passport from the age of 14

The Swiss identity card is issued to any citizen. It is not mandatory to carry, but it or a passport is needed in some situations. Driver's licenses are not always valid as identity document as they don't expire and can be old
Compulsory for citizens and permanent residents with a price of 10,000 SLL every 5 years
Distribution of national ID cards started in 2015 and the card is compulsory for all national citizens aged 16 and above
Identity cards have been used since 1949, and been compulsory since 1980. Children are required to obtain their first identity card at age 11, and must change to an adult identity card at age 18
The Paraguayan national identity card is issued by the National Police and is compulsory for all citizens; with a cost of 8500 Paraguayan guaraní
First issued and is compulsory after turning the age of 14. The new Bulgarian ID cards were introduced in 1999
Compulsory for citizens 16 and older permanently residing in Serbia, and compulsory for non-citizens residing in Serbia. Optional for minors 10–15
Every citizen 18 years or older must carry this ID card

Compulsory for citizens and permanent residents 15 and older and must be renewed upon turning 30 and upon turning 55 if born after January 1962. The NRIC does not need to be carried at all times, and it need not be produced to police officers who are merely screening passers-b…

All Lebanese are obliged by law to carry their identity cards with them at all times and are subject to fines should they not. As of 30 June 2006, all Lebanese nationals must hold the new magnetic Identification Card
New biometric national identity card have been rolled out in the late 2017
It is compulsory for all citizens at age 16, and there are penalties for not obtaining it within one month of turning 16 or obtaining citizenship, whichever comes last
A national identity card exists, usable all over the EU and a number of other countries, but commonly people use their driving licences or passports as ID
Compulsory at 15. Biometric since 2013, with information displayed in Arabic, French and English
Compulsory for citizens 15 and older and is used to identify the bearer in daily interaction with authorities
Every citizen immediately must carry an ID card after turning 18

All residents of Kuwait must have a Civil ID card. The legal ascendant(s) of newborns should apply for registration of the child within 60 days after birth. An expatriate must apply for a civil ID card within 30 days of getting his residency
Cedula de Identidad. Required at 12 (cedula juvenil) and 18 years of age. Panamanian citizens must carry their Cedula at all times. New biometric national identity cards rolling out in 2019
The Croatian identity card is compulsory for citizens of Croatia who have a permanent residence in Croatia and are at least 18 years old. By law, it must to be carried at all times
Compulsory for all Eritrean citizens. New version rolled out in 2014
The national identity card is compulsory for all Mongol citizens. Electronic since 2012, with informations displayed both in Mongol and English
The Identity document (previously known as "Cédula de idenitdad"), are issued to all Uruguayan citizens and legal residents, Required for children older than 45 day
As of 2014 the government has issued a Qatari ID Card to every Qatari citizen and resident over the age of 15
Compulsory for all Namibia citizens. New identity cards replaced previous “SWA” IDs in 2016
Compulsory at 16 and is to be carried at all times after turning 18.
Compulsory upon 16 years old and costs 1200 lekë (€10).

It is compulsory for all citizens at age 16, and there are penalties for not obtaining it within one month of turning 16 or obtaining citizenship, whichever comes last. Includes the image of the individual (no headgear or eyewear), their particulars, and their right thumbprint…
Compulsory for all national citizens. ID cards were implemented in 2013

Osebna izkaznica (identity card) is issued for citizens 18 and older who have a permanent residence in Slovenia who do not have a passport Citizens younger than 18 may obtain an identity card with their legal ascendant(s) permission. It must be carried at all times
An ID or passport is mandatory for a citizen of Latvia or a non-citizen who lives in Latvia and has reached 18
It is compulsory at the age of 18
In order to avail basic or any services, carry out financial transactions one must have CPR

The Elections and Boundaries Commission (EBC) is responsible for the issuing of National Identification Cards. A National Identification (ID) Card is issued to a citizen or eligible resident when they register to vote Eligible for the card are citizens of Trinidad and Tobago o…
Compulsory for all East Timorese citizens. Issued since 2018, with EU and Portuguese funds
Compulsory by law, but there is no penalty for not having one. Citizens carrying ID cards are not required to carry drivers licence and registration
Every Mauritian citizen who has reached 18 years old has to apply for a National ID card, which is one of the few accepted forms of identification, including a passport
Compulsory for all Djiboutians. Electronic since 2014
The Guyanese national identity card is an electronic ID card, compulsory for all Guyanese nationals
The Bhutanese national identity card is an electronic ID card, compulsory for all Bhutanese nationals and costs 100 Bhutanese ngultrum
It is compulsory for all Macau residents at the age of 5
First issued at age 15 and only issued to Luxembourg citizens, who are required by law to carry it at all times
Compulsory at the age of 16, but can be issued at 14 and has to be carried at all times after turning 18
Issued at 14, updated at 16, compulsory at 18
New biometric credit-sized passport cards replaced both driving licenses, health insurance cards and certain types of credit cards. They are compulsory for acquiring a passport
The Cape Verdian national identity card (referred as “Citizen card”) is an electronic biometric ID card, compulsory for all Cape Verdian nationals
Compulsory for all citizens at the age of 12
Optional, although compulsory for voting and other government transactions New biometric national ID cards were released since June 2022
Mandatory national identity card was decided in Kiribati in 2018 and introduced soon after
Compulsory for all Seychelles citizens, with a cost of SR50
The Antiguan and Barbudan national identity card is compulsory for voting as well as for different government transactions
The Dominica national multpurpose identitification card is optional for all Dominiquais nationals and is valid for international travel within OECS countries
Compulsory for all Sanmarinese citizens. Biometric and valid for international travel since 2016
